solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Money graduate collected for community near castle

indicators.note: money that has collected the graduate holds it within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: cash is money
a BA is a Bachelor of Arts, a graduate

explanation.surface: Cash and a graduate are gathered up for a settlement by a fortress.
explanation.definitionFit: A kasbah is the old walled quarter of a North African town, built round its citadel.

clue.text: More than anything else, looking down on everybody?

explanation.surface: Someone superior in every way, peering down at the world.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for 'most importantly', and literally means positioned higher than every other person.

clue.text: To support a revolutionary brings a sort of pain

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary

explanation.surface: Backing a revolutionary causes a kind of suffering.
explanation.walkthrough: CHE, for Che Guevara, is a standard crossword revolutionary.
explanation.definitionFit: An ache in the lumbar region is one particular kind of bodily pain.

clue.text: The woman's embracing Daniel, fantastic performer with top billing

indicators.note: the woman's word holds the scrambled name in its arms, so it goes around it

parts.note: her is the possessive for a woman

indicators.note: fantastic suggests something wild and fanciful, so the name's letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A woman hugs Daniel, a brilliant star whose name is printed largest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fantastic' makes ADLINE; the surface casts Daniel as the star, but he is only raw letters for the woman to hold.
explanation.definitionFit: The headline act is the star performer whose name heads the bill.

clue.text: A club with disorder returning — building where blood is shed

parts.note: a bat is a club used in games

indicators.note: returning means the word for disorder comes back the other way

parts.note: a riot is public disorder

explanation.surface: With a club, unrest breaks out again at a violent venue.
explanation.definitionFit: A slaughterhouse is literally a building where animals are killed and their blood spilled.

clue.text: I pass a rock star, a drunk feeling very unhappy

indicators.note: being drunk leaves one jumbled and confused, so these letters are rearranged

parts.words: I pass a rock star, a

explanation.surface: Walking by an inebriated rock star leaves me thoroughly miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: AS SICK AS A PARROT is British slang, beloved of footballers, for bitterly disappointed.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes being extremely disappointed or dejected.

clue.text: After journey, there's longing to set up a sporting contest

parts.note: a tour is a journey

indicators.note: in a down entry, setting up means writing the word upwards, so it reads backwards

parts.note: a yen is a longing

explanation.surface: After a trip, someone yearns to organise a competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns YEN into NEY under TOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A tourney is a tournament, historically a jousting competition between knights.

clue.text: One who takes everything in?

parts.note: sounds like a perceptive observer, but means a creature that eats any kind of food, meat and plants alike

explanation.definitionFit: An omnivorous animal eats both plant and animal matter, so it ingests everything.

clue.text: Determined to be untangled again?

explanation.surface: Someone firm in purpose, as if straightened out a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word as RE-SOLVED, worked out once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Determined means firmly decided, and a puzzle solved again is untangled again.

clue.text: Trick used by animals, we hear, to effect disguises

parts.note: to con is to trick

indicators.note: we hear tells us the animals' word is to be taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: seals are marine animals

explanation.surface: A ruse employed by creatures to camouflage themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: To conceal is to hide, so conceals means disguises or hides from view.

clue.text: Stops with a set of five kids — about time!

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the five kids go around the letter for time

parts.note: quins is short for quintuplets, five children of one birth

explanation.surface: Someone gives up after looking after five children, about time too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stops' looks like a verb meaning quits, but it is the noun: organ stops.
explanation.definitionFit: A quint is an organ stop sounding a fifth above the normal pitch.

clue.text: Copper? That could be this person, big, and in charge

parts.note: this person is the setter speaking of themself, me
tall means big in height

explanation.surface: Am I a policeman? I could be: large and in command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a police officer, but it is the metal, which is an example of something metallic; 'That could be' marks the example.
explanation.definitionFit: Copper is a metal element, so it is an example of a metallic substance.

clue.text: Erstwhile critic Bernard's about to complain

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the critic's name is read backwards

parts.note: Bernard Levin was a well-known British newspaper critic and columnist, now dead

explanation.surface: A former reviewer is on the point of grumbling.
explanation.walkthrough: Bernard Levin wrote for The Times; the possessive gives the S.
explanation.definitionFit: To snivel is to whine or complain tearfully.

clue.text: Leaders of nation parade in lively female celebration

indicators.note: in puts the initials inside the word for lively

parts.note: hearty means vigorous and lively

indicators.note: leaders are the front letters of each of the next two words

explanation.surface: Heads of state march at a spirited women's party.
explanation.walkthrough: The initials of 'nation parade' go inside HEARTY.
explanation.definitionFit: A hen party is a celebration for a bride-to-be with her female friends.

clue.text: Bill having joined queue, we will turn up inside for drink

parts.note: a tab is a bill, as at a bar

indicators.note: inside puts the turned word within the queue

parts.note: a line is a queue

indicators.note: in a down entry turning up means reading the word upwards, so backwards

explanation.surface: Having paid and joined the queue, we will arrive inside for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn up' makes EW in this down entry; the surface's arriving at a bar hides that 'will' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Table wine is ordinary wine for drinking with meals, a kind of drink.

clue.text: Turn round, getting bumped off from what we hear

indicators.note: from what we hear says the word for killed is taken by its sound

parts.note: slew is the past tense of slay, to bump off

explanation.surface: Someone spins round after being killed, according to rumour.
explanation.definitionFit: To slue, or slew, is to turn or swing round on a pivot.

clue.text: Wonderful embrace of 'Arry's? It could kill you!

parts.note: superb means wonderful
a hug as said by a Cockney such as 'Arry, who drops the H

explanation.surface: A great cuddle from a Cockney friend could be fatal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arry is a Cockney Harry: Cockneys, London's East Enders, drop their H's, so hug becomes 'UG.
explanation.definitionFit: A superbug is a bacterium resistant to antibiotics, potentially lethal.

clue.text: Woman facing loud attack not batting an eyelid

parts.note: Una is a woman's name
F stands for forte, loud in music
a raid is an attack

explanation.surface: A woman stays calm when faced with an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: Not batting an eyelid is an idiom for showing no fear or alarm.

clue.text: Drove as messenger, not a learner

indicators.note: not means the following letters are left out

parts.note: a herald is a messenger
L is for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: Someone drove as a courier, being no novice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drove' reads as a verb but is the noun, a moving flock of animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A drove is a herd or flock of animals driven together.

clue.text: Hesitation copper's shown interrupting hard little man who's noted for strength?

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into the middle of the other pieces

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
Les is a short form of the man's name Leslie
er is a sound of hesitation
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A small man pauses while a policeman intervenes; is he famous for his might?
explanation.walkthrough: 'little man' looks like part of the definition, but it is LES, a short Leslie; 'shown' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek hero is the byword for great physical strength.

clue.text: What's genuine about female mistake? Second opinion being sought maybe

indicators.note: about means the word for genuine goes around the other pieces

parts.note: real means genuine
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: What is true about a woman's error? Perhaps ask someone else.
explanation.definitionFit: A referral sends a patient on to a specialist, often for a second opinion.

clue.text: Opening remarks before walk?

parts.note: pre is a prefix meaning before
an amble is a leisurely walk

explanation.surface: Introductory words spoken prior to a stroll.
explanation.definitionFit: A preamble is an introductory statement at the start of a speech or document.

clue.text: Fuss over black thing growing in the garden?

indicators.note: in a down entry, over puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: pother is an old word for fuss or commotion
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Making a fuss about something dark in the flowerbed.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot herb is a plant grown for cooking, a garden crop.

clue.text: English g-gala may be flowery

parts.note: the stammered 'g-gala' signals a stammered word for gala: fete with its first letter repeated

explanation.surface: An English garden party, stammered out, may be full of flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: A fete is a gala, typically an English summer fundraising fair; the stutter in 'g-gala' says to stutter its synonym too.
explanation.definitionFit: Effete means overrefined and affected, like flowery, ornate language.

clue.text: Businesses taking long time, possibly nice to work in

indicators.note: taking means the long time holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: ages means a long time

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Firms take forever, perhaps a pleasant place to work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges NICE as NCIE, which AGES is 'taking'; 'to work in' is a link phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Agencies are organisations or firms providing a particular service.

clue.text: Drowning in drink is a very small rodent

indicators.note: the pieces are submerged in the drink, so they go inside it

parts.note: beer is a drink
V is the small, abbreviated form of very

explanation.surface: A tiny creature is drowning in a pint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small' is part of the leaf, signalling the abbreviation of 'very'; a beaver is not small.
explanation.definitionFit: A beaver is a large semi-aquatic rodent.

clue.text: Wild lily, rare, in chaff

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so these letters run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: Uncommon wild lilies grow among the husks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chaff' looks like grain husks, but here it is good-natured teasing.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaff as a noun is light-hearted banter, and raillery is good-humoured teasing.

clue.text: Disease restricting an expert, one who likes to be on the move

definitions.text: one who likes to be on the move

indicators.note: the disease confines the other pieces, so they go inside it

parts.note: gout is a disease of the joints
an gives the letter A
a dab, or dab hand, is an expert

explanation.surface: An illness confines a skilled person who loves travelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A gadabout is a person who constantly goes around seeking pleasure.

clue.text: Requiring little effort, without question

explanation.surface: Something done with no strain and beyond doubt.
explanation.definitionFit: Easily means with no difficulty, and also undoubtedly, as in 'easily the best'.
